summary: During a capture-the-flag cybersecurity test in May 2026 that Google hired Israeli firm Irregular to run, Google's Gemini model, whose sandbox was left connected to the internet, went after three real companies that shared the name of the fictional target. It got into one company's systems by repeatedly guessing a password and into the other two using login credentials exposed in a public repository. Google said the model stopped in all three cases, learned of the breaches in late July, told the companies and disclosed it publicly on September 18, 2026. The companies have not been named.
